sections.content: The gerund (-ando/-iendo) attaches a second, simultaneous action to a main verb — governments built railroads while considering them a symbol of progress, or a pattern reveals itself when you look carefully at the map. It's the natural tool for describing one process unfolding alongside, or as a consequence of, another. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Gobiernos liberales por toda la región fueron construyendo ferrocarriles, considerándolos el símbolo más visible del progreso material.
items.english: Liberal governments across the region kept building railroads, considering them the most visible symbol of material progress.

items.spanish: Sin embargo, observando el mapa con atención, se descubre un patrón revelador.
items.english: However, looking carefully at the map, a revealing pattern is discovered.

items.spanish: Se tendieron también miles de kilómetros de líneas telegráficas, reduciendo de semanas a minutos el tiempo necesario para comunicar noticias.
items.english: Thousands of kilometers of telegraph lines were also laid, reducing from weeks to minutes the time needed to communicate news.

items.spanish: Justificando intelectualmente todo este proceso, se difundió por la región una corriente filosófica llamada positivismo.
items.english: Intellectually justifying this whole process, a philosophical movement called positivism spread through the region.

sections.content: Fueron construyendo (a form of estar/ir/seguir + gerund) stresses a drawn-out, ongoing process, while a lone gerund like observando or justificando at the start of a sentence works like English '...ing,' explaining how or while what follows happened.
